ex: 16% azelaic acid for breakouts and the redness that comes with them.
d: Azelaic acid is the rare active that works on spots, redness and dark marks at once, which makes it the sensible choice when skin is doing all three.
At 16% this is a clinical-strength dose, buffered with panthenol so it stays usable daily.
caution: Introduce slowly. A light tingle on first use is normal; stop if it stings.

n: Seoul 1988 Royal Skin Glow Serum - Niacinamide 70% + Yuja
ex: A high-niacinamide glow serum with Korean citron.
d: Niacinamide at this concentration works on tone, pores and barrier strength together, which is why it is the one active almost every routine can carry.
Yuja adds the vitamin C side of brightening without the sting of a pure ascorbic serum.

ex: A collagen booster in a click pen, for a lit finish.
d: The pen format means a measured dose each time rather than a pipette guess, which matters with a serum you use on the whole face.
Collagen and peptides for bounce; the glow shows up long before the firmness does.
bn: Measured dose from the click pen

ex: The serum that started Medicube's kojic acid line.
d: Kojic acid interrupts pigment at the source and turmeric handles the inflammation that keeps marks coming back, which is the pairing dark marks actually need.
Niacinamide underneath keeps the whole thing tolerable for daily use.
bn: Fades dark spots and post-acne marks
Turmeric calms the inflammation behind marks

ex: Retinal, the faster cousin of retinol, in a small booster tube.
d: Retinal converts to the active form in one step instead of two, so results on lines and texture arrive sooner than with retinol.
A booster rather than a full serum: a short course, then back to your usual routine.
bn: Small tube for a focused course
caution: Use at night only, two to three times a week to begin. Sunscreen is essential while using retinal.

ex: Vitamin C for people whose skin hates vitamin C.
d: A stable derivative rather than pure ascorbic acid, so you get the brightening without the sting, the flush or the bottle turning brown.
Gentle enough to use every morning from the first week.
bn: Stable - it will not oxidise in the bottle

ex: Glutathione and vitamin C, in the brightening number of the range.
d: Glutathione is the brightening ingredient people usually look for in a supplement, concentrated here into a serum that works where you can see it.
The dark glass bottle is doing a job: these ingredients degrade in light.
bn: Works on dark marks over time

ex: 70% peach extract and niacinamide for a soft, even glow.
d: Anua's peach line is the gentler sibling of the heartleaf one: the same restraint, aimed at tone rather than redness.
Niacinamide handles the pores while the peach extract keeps skin comfortable.

n: Seoul 1988 Serum - Retinal Liposome 2% + Black Ginseng
ex: Liposomal retinal with black ginseng for firmness.
d: Wrapping retinal in liposomes slows the release, so you get the results on lines without the peeling week that usually comes first.
Black ginseng is the hanbang half: traditional, warming, and good for skin that looks tired.
caution: Night use only. Build up slowly and wear sunscreen every day.

ex: A calming essence for the step before everything else.
d: Thin enough to be a first treatment and calming enough to be the only one on a bad skin day.
Built around centella and panthenol, with nothing in it that could set reactive skin off.
bn: Preps skin for the rest of the routine

n: Lush Blush NAD+ Peptide Boosting Serum
ex: The serum in the NAD+ pair, for tired, flat-looking skin.
d: NAD+ works on the energy side of ageing rather than the surface, so the change shows up as skin that looks awake rather than skin that looks coated.
Use it under the matching cream for the full course.

ex: A vitamin serum that gives an immediate filter-like glow.
d: Named for what it does on camera: skin reads smoother and brighter straight away, with the vitamin work happening underneath over weeks.
Good under makeup, better on a bare face.

ex: Rice and ceramides, for a barrier that needs feeding.
d: Rice water has been Korean skincare's quiet brightener for centuries; the ceramides are the modern half, patching a barrier that has stopped holding water.
A serum you can use twice a day without thinking about it.

ex: Three forms of collagen in one pump bottle.
d: Different collagen molecule sizes reach different depths, which is the argument for using three rather than one.
The texture is milky and light, so it works as a daily serum rather than a treat.
bn: Three collagen types at three depths

ex: The softening number: fermented rice for rough, tight skin.
d: Fermentation breaks ingredients down into forms skin takes up more easily, which is why this reads smoother after one use rather than one month.
The texture people describe as a softening toner-serum hybrid.

n: Tea Purity 99% Tea Niacinamide Toning Shot BP Serum
ex: 99% green tea with niacinamide, for oily skin with marks.
d: Green tea instead of water as the base, which is where the 99% comes from, with niacinamide and a touch of BHA doing the work on pores.
Built for the skin that breaks out and then keeps the mark for months.
bn: Green tea base calms as it works

ex: Bakuchiol, for skin that wants retinol results without retinol.
d: Bakuchiol does similar work on lines and firmness without the peeling, the sun sensitivity or the pregnancy warnings.
The plumping comes from hyaluronic acid, and it shows up immediately.
bn: Can be used morning and night

ex: Glutathione and tranexamic acid, aimed squarely at dark spots.
d: Two of the strongest non-prescription pigment ingredients in one bottle, which is why this is the serum to reach for when niacinamide alone has stopped making a difference.
Expect weeks, not days - that is how pigment works.
bn: Works on sun damage and melasma-type marks
caution: Daily sunscreen is not optional with this one - pigment comes straight back without it.

ex: A retinol serum with the barrier support built in.
d: Most retinol serums leave you to manage the dryness yourself; this one carries ceramides and niacinamide to take the edge off.
Still a retinol, so the usual rules apply.
caution: Night use only. Start twice a week. Wear sunscreen every day.

ex: The serum half of Purito's most trusted centella pair.
d: No fragrance, no essential oils, no colour - just centella in a concentration that actually does something about redness.
The serum to keep for the weeks when skin has turned on you.

ex: Rice at nearly half the bottle, for dull and dry skin.
d: I'm From build single-ingredient products, and the rice line is the one people buy twice: brightening that comes with moisture instead of at the cost of it.
Milky, slightly rich, and it sinks in completely.

ex: Pure ascorbic acid in dark glass, the way it should be sold.
d: Pure vitamin C is the gold standard for brightening and the hardest form to keep stable, which is why the bottle is small and brown.
Vitamin E and ferulic acid are there to hold it together and multiply the effect.
bn: The strongest form of vitamin C
caution: Use in the morning under sunscreen. Keep the bottle closed and out of light.

ex: 5% tranexamic acid for pigment that will not shift.
d: Tranexamic acid works on the pathway that drives melasma and stubborn sun marks, which is a different route from the brighteners most serums use.
At 5% it is a serious dose, so give it eight weeks before judging.
bn: Evens out tone across the face
caution: Daily sunscreen is essential, otherwise the marks return.

ex: Peptides and hyaluronic acid suspended as visible capsules.
d: The capsules are not decoration: they hold the peptides separate until the moment you use them.
Deep hydration first, firmness over the following weeks.

ex: 23% pure vitamin C - the strong one.
d: This is the high-dose end of vitamin C, for skin that has already got used to a gentler version and stopped seeing change.
Thick, slightly tacky, and it works.
caution: Not a starting point. A tingle is expected; patch test first and always wear sunscreen.

ex: Fermented bifida and the desert rose that survives on nothing.
d: Jericho rose is the plant that revives from completely dry, which is a neat image for what this serum is meant to do for dehydrated skin.
Fermented bifida does the repair work underneath.

ex: Propolis and niacinamide, the brand's most reordered serum.
d: Propolis is naturally antibacterial, which is why this suits skin that is dull and breaking out at the same time.
Slightly sticky going on, glowing within minutes.

n: Vitamin C Booster Shot Face and Eye Cream
ex: A vitamin C booster you can take right up to the eye.
d: Most vitamin C is too harsh for the eye area; this one is formulated for both, which saves a separate eye product.
15% vitamin C with glutathione behind it, in a small tube meant to be used up.

n: Madagascar Centella Retinol 0.2 Boosting Shot Ampoule
ex: Retinol at a beginner-friendly 0.2%, cushioned with centella.
d: 0.2% is the strength to start on, and the centella in the base is doing the job of the moisturiser you would otherwise need afterwards.
Squalane keeps it comfortable through the adjustment weeks.
caution: Night use only. Two nights a week to begin, and sunscreen every morning.

ex: Ginseng and snail mucin, for skin that looks worn out.
d: Snail mucin is the repair ingredient Korean skincare is best known for, and ginseng is the hanbang half that handles dullness and loss of bounce.
Thicker than their Glow serum, and better suited to night.
bn: Rich enough to end a night routine

ex: 10% niacinamide with tranexamic acid - the dark spot workhorse.
d: TIAM's reputation rests on this bottle: a high niacinamide dose paired with tranexamic acid and arbutin, which is close to what a dermatologist would layer themselves.
Not elegant, very effective.
caution: If you are new to niacinamide, start every other day.

n: Madagascar Centella Tender Cica Intensive Ampoule
ex: The strongest centella concentration in the range.
d: When the toner and cream are not enough, this is the ampoule that goes between them.
Dark glass, thick texture, and a noticeable drop in redness within days.
bn: Use as a course, then pull back

n: Madagascar Centella Tone Brightening Capsule Ampoule
ex: Brightening capsules in a centella base, so tone work stays gentle.
d: The brightening ampoule for people whose skin usually objects to brightening products.
Capsules keep the vitamins intact until you press them out on the skin.

ex: A minimal relief serum for skin that is over it.
d: The name is the formula: ceramide 3, panthenol and centella, with very little else in the bottle.
For the weeks after too much exfoliation, too much sun, or a product that went wrong.
bn: Short formula, nothing to react to

ex: 1% kojic acid, targeted at dark spots and pigmentation.
d: Kojic acid is derived from fermented rice and blocks pigment production directly, which makes it one of the more reliable options for dark marks.
Paired with niacinamide so the effect compounds rather than irritates.
caution: Wear sunscreen daily while using kojic acid.

ex: Hyaluronic acid and centella in the blue bottle of the range.
d: The hydrating member of the centella family: water first, calming second, with nothing heavy left behind.
The one to use in the morning, under sunscreen, every day.

ex: 70% deep sea water, for skin that is dehydrated rather than dry.
d: Dehydrated skin needs minerals and water rather than oil, which is exactly what deep sea water brings.
Light, almost watery, and it disappears on contact.
